neighbours.label: the comma or 'or' between alternative channels something travels through (by road, rail or ship; over copper, fiber or radio; print, online or TV)
fire: The parcels can be shipped by air, truck, rail, or courier.
Customers reach the bank through branches, telephone, mobile apps or mail.
News now reaches us through newspapers, radio, cable, and the web.
Power is carried over wires, cables or microwave links.
The pilgrims arrived on foot, by mule, by boat, or by coach.
Music is sold on vinyl, cassette, CD and streaming services.
Messages were sent by courier, pigeon, telegraph or wireless.
Water reaches the fields through canals, pipes, or ditches.
quiet: The parcels contained socks, gloves, scarves, or hats.
Customers of the bank include teachers, nurses, farmers and clerks.
News of the storm reached Denver, Omaha, Tulsa, and Memphis.
Power tools can be loud, heavy, or awkward.
The pilgrims sang, prayed, ate, and slept.
Music lessons are offered in piano, guitar, drums and voice.
Messages were written in Latin, Greek, Arabic or Persian.
Water in the fields looked cold, muddy, or green.

notes: The peak token is mostly a list comma, but lists of cities, languages, sports, foods and adjectives stay low, while transport, signal and media lists fire. A list of religions and one of operating systems also fired, so the channel reading may be too narrow.
